baseline_prompt_en: A photographic editorial staged in a 1935-inspired Korean café reading room, explicitly a later interwar interior. One adult woman with the reference portrait’s long dark wavy hair, softly oval face, dark eyes and natural lip shape sits at a small walnut table. She wears an ivory blouse under a burgundy sleeveless knit vest. She pauses a turning newspaper page to listen to a tabletop gramophone: her right fingers pinch the lifted upper page corner while her left palm holds the lower newspaper flat, and her eyes turn toward the gramophone. The lifted page makes a clear diagonal above the spread. On the same table, a dark shellac disc rests on the gramophone turntable with its tonearm lowered onto the outer groove; its small flared brass horn points toward her. A porcelain coffee cup and brass sugar tongs occupy the near edge, separated from the newspaper. Behind her are bentwood chairs, dark timber wall panels and a modest geometric frosted-glass partition. A sunlit window with outside drizzle gives fine bright droplets and warm reflected light across the paper. Frame a three-quarter seated portrait with face, both hands, newspaper and entire gramophone legible together. Keep the scene’s later café modernity evident through the fitted knit layering, compact sound apparatus and geometric interior. Prioritize the suspended page-turn listening action, the distinct interwar café material language, and visible reference appearance. Natural skin texture, credible hand contact, nuanced wood and brass, quiet photographic realism.
